unit_title: Me, Myself and My Future Job
subtitle: Talking About Jobs and Careers, Modals (Can, May, Should), Future Forms (Will & Going to), and Safety Rules at Work

stories.summary: Helen explains how she crafts rings, necklaces, and earrings from precious stones using delicate hand tools and lasers.
stories.narrative: Helen is a creative jewellery designer in Thessaloniki. She takes metal and precious stones and creates rings, necklaces, earrings and other fine jewellery. She can use loads of hand tools to make delicate pieces. Her artistic work requires attention to detail, finger dexterity, patience, and good hand-eye co-ordination. Artistic ability and fashion knowledge are very important in this rewarding craft.

landmarks.desc: Precision pliers, files, hammers, and laser cutters used to craft intricate metalwork.

landmarks.name: Precious Stones & Metal Rings
landmarks.desc: Sparkling diamonds, rubies, and gold bands shaped into bespoke jewellery.

landmarks.name: Hand-Eye Co-ordination Bench
landmarks.desc: The workbench requiring intense concentration, steady hands, and fine finger dexterity.

stories.summary: Sophia manages aircraft movements from the radar tower, coordinating schedules and communicating across time zones.
stories.narrative: Sophia is an air traffic controller at a busy airport. Her job is to co-ordinate the movement of aeroplanes and direct them to keep flying schedules on time. She handles every plane that is taking off or landing. She usually works forty-hour weeks, including night and weekend shifts. It is a stressful occupation that requires clear speech, communication skills, Mathematics, and foreign languages for a successful career.

landmarks.desc: The elevated observation cab equipped with panoramic radar displays and radio links.

landmarks.name: Flight Schedules Monitor
landmarks.desc: Real-time departure and arrival boards ensuring aeroplanes maintain strict airway separation.

landmarks.name: Radio Communication Headset
landmarks.desc: Crystal-clear microphone and audio gear for radio telephony with international pilots.

landmarks.name: Multi-Lingual Radar Ops
landmarks.desc: Standardized aviation English and foreign language proficiency essential during busy shifts.

stories.summary: George visits recovering patients at home, providing medical assistance, emotional cheer, and dietary advice.
stories.narrative: George is a home health nurse who travels to different locations to care for ill patients. He instructs family members on how to look after the sick patient with love and patience. George is responsible, compassionate, and cheerful, bringing comfort to everyone he visits. In his studies, classes in Biology, Health Sciences, Home Economics, and Nutrition prepared him to help people every day.

landmarks.name: Home Patient Care Kit
landmarks.desc: A travel bag packed with stethoscopes, bandages, blood pressure monitors, and thermometer kits.

landmarks.name: Compassionate Bedside Consultation
landmarks.desc: Warm, encouraging medical visits for elderly or convalescent citizens in their residences.

landmarks.name: Nutrition & Meal Guidance
landmarks.desc: Customized dietary recommendations derived from home economics and clinical nutrition.

landmarks.name: Mobile Community Care
landmarks.desc: Travelling to diverse suburban and rural locations to offer essential nursing support.

stories.summary: Vassilis showcases styling tools in the salon while Maria explains ecological fieldwork and Amazon research.
stories.narrative: Vassilis is a hairdresser who cuts and styles hair using a variety of tools such as scissors, razors, and hot dryers. He can colour, perm, or straighten hair, and he must be creative and self-confident. Chemistry and science courses are helpful in his salon. Maria is an ecologist who studies nature. She works in a lab but also goes out to the mountain area to study wild plants and animals. She loves volunteer work and will travel to the Amazon. Working independently or as part of a cooperative team are essential skills for her profession.

landmarks.name: Professional Styling Station
landmarks.desc: Precision salon scissors, electric dryers, conditioning lotions, and straighteners.

landmarks.name: Chemistry & Hair Treatments
landmarks.desc: Chemical solutions formulated to safely colour, perm, or straighten diverse hair textures.

landmarks.name: Ecology Fieldwork Station
landmarks.desc: Collecting botanical specimens and monitoring wildlife in endangered forest ecosystems.

landmarks.name: Amazon Conservation Research
landmarks.desc: International conservation teamwork protecting biodiversity and freshwater river basins.

grammar_lab.title: Inductive Grammar Lab: Modals & Future Intentions
grammar_lab.subtitle: Discover how English expresses ability, permission, possibility, advice, promises, and future career plans.
target_structures: Future with Will: predictions, promises, warnings, spontaneous decisions
Future with Going to: intentions and pre-arranged future plans
Safety Rules at Work: imperative warnings and protective equipment

rules.use: Expressing ability ('can'), possibility or polite permission ('may'), and recommended advice ('should').
examples: Ecologists can work in a lab or outdoors in nature. (Ability & possibility)
You should be brave and well trained to be a lifeguard. (Advice / requirement)
May I ask for more information about the job? (Polite permission)

rules.structure: Future: will vs be going to
rules.use: 'Will' for sudden decisions, predictions, and promises; 'Going to' for intentions and pre-arranged goals.
examples: I will study hard for my exams, I promise! (Promise)
Next summer, I am going to travel to the Amazon to study plants. (Pre-arranged intention)

rules.use: Imperatives and modal prohibitions to ensure safety in labs, factories, and supermarkets.
examples: Always wear safety goggles in the chemistry laboratory.
Keep supermarket aisles clear of empty boxes to prevent accidents.

practice_items.prompt: Lifeguards ________ swim fast and stay calm under pressure.
practice_items.explanation: Modal expressions of ability take the bare infinitive without 'to'.

practice_items.prompt: The phone is ringing in the office! — Don't worry, I ________ it!
practice_items.explanation: We use 'will' for spontaneous on-the-spot decisions made at the moment of speaking.

practice_items.prompt: Maria ________ travel to the Amazon next summer; her tickets are booked.
practice_items.explanation: 'Be going to' expresses pre-arranged intentions and plans formed prior to speaking.

practice_items.prompt: You ________ wear protective goggles whenever handling dangerous chemicals.
practice_items.explanation: 'Should' conveys strong advisability and essential safety recommendations.

practice_items.prompt: Never ________ with running machinery or electrical switches in the factory.
practice_items.explanation: Imperative negative safety instructions use 'Never + bare infinitive'.

school_lab_listening.title: Career Day Thessaloniki: Asking for Job Information
school_lab_listening.context: Listen to a telephone conversation between a job applicant inquiring about a lifeguard position and the personnel manager.

script_lines.speaker: Applicant
script_lines.text: Hello, my name is Kostas. I am calling about the lifeguard job at Alimos beach.

script_lines.speaker: Manager
script_lines.text: Hello Kostas! Are you strong and healthy? Can you swim fast and dive well?

script_lines.speaker: Applicant
script_lines.text: Yes, I have been a competitive swimmer for five years and I have a first aid certificate.

script_lines.speaker: Manager
script_lines.text: Excellent. The job can be dangerous, so you should be brave and well trained. You may need to save people in difficult conditions. You will work six hours a day and you can use the beach facilities.

script_lines.speaker: Applicant
script_lines.text: That sounds fantastic. When can I come for a personal interview?

script_lines.speaker: Manager
script_lines.text: Come tomorrow morning at 10 o'clock. Bring your certificate and ID card.

content_true_false.statement: An air traffic controller usually works forty-hour weeks including night shifts.
content_true_false.feedback: Correct! Sophia explains that controllers work rotational shifts to keep skies safe 24/7.

content_true_false.statement: A jewellery designer only uses heavy hammers and never touches computers.
content_true_false.feedback: False! Helen uses modern computers and laser technology alongside delicate hand tools.

content_true_false.statement: Home health nurses only work inside large hospitals and never travel to homes.
content_true_false.feedback: False! Home health nurses specifically travel to patients' homes to provide dedicated care.

content_true_false.statement: Workers must keep supermarket aisles clear of boxes to prevent tripping accidents.
content_true_false.feedback: True! Keeping passageways clear is a vital workplace safety rule.

content_true_false.statement: Ecologists study plants and animals in both laboratories and outdoor environments.
content_true_false.feedback: True! Maria works in scientific labs and in wild natural habitats like the Amazon.

writing_workshop.title: Guided Job Profile Workshop: My Future Career
writing_workshop.guidance: Follow the structured framework to write a comprehensive job profile outlining daily duties, necessary skills, school subjects, and personal goals.

sections.title: 1. Job Title & Workplace Environment
sections.prompt: State the profession you want to follow and where professionals in this field work.
connector_bank: In the future I would like to become
Professionals in this field work in
sections.model_snippet: In the future, I would like to become an ecologist. Ecologists work in research laboratories and out in wild natural areas like forests, rivers, and national parks.

sections.title: 2. Daily Duties & Responsibilities
sections.prompt: Explain what you will do day-to-day and what equipment you can use.
connector_bank: They can use a variety of tools such as
sections.model_snippet: Their main duty is to study wild plants and animals and protect natural habitats. They can use microscopes, water sampling kits, and computer models to track environmental health.

sections.title: 3. Required Skills & School Subjects
sections.prompt: Highlight the personality traits, skills, and school courses necessary for this career.
connector_bank: To do this job well, you should be
sections.model_snippet: To do this job well, you should be patient, hardworking, and observant. You must have good communication skills and team spirit. Helpful school subjects are Biology, Chemistry, and Foreign Languages.

sections.title: 4. Future Goals & New Year Resolutions
sections.prompt: State what you are going to do to prepare for this future career.
connector_bank: Next year, I am going to
sections.model_snippet: Next year, I am going to join the school environmental club and do volunteer work planting trees. I will study hard in science to achieve my dream!

teacher_notes.topic: Grammar: Modal Functions in Career Guidance
teacher_notes.detail: Clarify for pupils that 'can' conveys physical or learned ability, 'may' expresses formal possibility or polite permission, and 'should' offers constructive advice or professional recommendations.
Distinguish between 'will' for spontaneous on-the-spot decisions, predictions based on opinion, and promises, versus 'be going to' for established personal intentions and pre-arranged future plans.
